text:
The Girl Who Loved the Rain

Aarav had never believed in love at first sight.

He believed in timing, conversations, and the slow way strangers become home.

One rainy afternoon, while hiding inside a small library from the storm, he noticed a girl sitting by the window. She wasn't reading the book in her hands. She was watching the raindrops race down the glass, smiling as if the rain were telling her a secret.

Her name was Mira.

The first thing they ever said to each other was about a missing bookmark.

The second was about coffee.

The third lasted four hours.

Days became weeks, and somehow they kept meeting—at the library, at the café across the street, at the park where the old banyan tree stood. They learned each other's little habits.

Mira always laughed before telling a joke.

Aarav always remembered everyone's favorite song.

She loved sunsets.

He loved sunrises.

So they agreed to watch both together.

When Mira was afraid of failing her exams, Aarav stayed awake all night helping her study.

When Aarav lost confidence in himself, Mira reminded him of every dream he had almost forgotten.

Neither tried to change the other.

Instead, they helped each other become the best versions of themselves.

Years passed.

Life became busier. There were misunderstandings, long-distance days, missed calls, and silent nights. More than once, they wondered if love was enough.

But every time one stepped back, the other stepped forward.

Not because their relationship was perfect.

Because they chose each other, again and again.

One evening, they returned to the same library where they had first met.

The rain had started just like it had years ago.

Aarav smiled and held out an old bookmark.

"I think this belongs to you."

Mira laughed.

"I've been looking for it for years."

He knelt down, holding a small velvet box.

"I don't promise a life without storms," he said softly. "I promise I'll stand beside you in every one of them."

With tears in her eyes, she whispered, "Yes."

They married the following spring.

Their home was never the biggest or the fanciest, but it was always full of music, books, plants, laughter, and the smell of fresh tea after the rain.

When they grew old, their hair turned silver, and their hands became wrinkled.

Every monsoon, they still sat by the same window.

Watching raindrops race down the glass.

Just like the day they met.

One afternoon, their granddaughter asked,

"What is the secret to true love?"

Mira smiled at Aarav.

He smiled back.

And together they answered,

"Love isn't finding the perfect person.

It's choosing the same imperfect person every single day—and making them feel loved, no matter what."

Outside, the rain continued to fall.

Inside, two hearts that had once been strangers still felt like home.

The End.
